question: The Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, which was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 17 December 2024, amends how many Acts?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill** was introduced in the Lok Sabha on **17 December 2024**.
 
• This Bill amends **three Acts**, which pertain to the administration and governance of Union Territories in India.
 
• The primary aim of this amendment is to ensure better legal frameworks for the Union Territories, enhancing administrative efficiency and governance structures.
 
• Union Territories are governed directly by the Central Government, and the amendment ensures alignment with evolving governance needs and legislative requirements.
 
• **Option 1** is correct as the Bill specifically targets amendments in three specific Acts associated with Union Territories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Union Territories in India:**

 
 
• Union Territories are administrative units governed by the Central Government, unlike states which have their own elected governments.
 
• India currently has **8 Union Territories**, including Delhi, Chandigarh, Jammu & Kashmir, and Puducherry.
 
• Union Territories often have special legislative needs due to their unique administrative arrangements.
 
 
 
• **Acts Governing Union Territories:**
 
 
• Union Territories are administered under specific laws passed by the Parliament of India.
 
• These laws define governance structures, powers of administrators, and the role of the Central Government in day-to-day administration.
 
• Some Union Territories, like Delhi and Puducherry, have legislatures but limited powers compared to states.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Amendments:**
 
 
• Amendments to Acts are carried out to address legal gaps, improve administrative efficiency, and cater to evolving governance challenges.
 
• The Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill is an example of such legislative action aimed at improving governance frameworks.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Governance in Union Territories:**
 
 
• Efficient governance ensures that Union Territories are able to cater to the needs of their residents effectively.
 
• Union Territories often serve as hubs for economic activities due to their strategic locations (e.g., Delhi and Chandigarh).
 
• Legal amendments help streamline administrative processes and remove ambiguities in laws.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Parliament:**

 
 
• The Parliament of India has exclusive powers to legislate for Union Territories under Article 246 of the Constitution.
 
• Parliament can create, abolish, or merge Union Territories based on legislative needs and administrative requirements.
 
 
 
• **Governance Challenges:**
 
 
• Union Territories often face challenges such as limited autonomy and dependence on Central Government for resources.
 
• Legislative amendments aim to address these challenges by providing better frameworks for administration.
 
 
 
• **Delhi and Puducherry:**
 
 
• These Union Territories have elected legislative assemblies, but their powers are curtailed under specific laws.
 
• For instance, the Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi Act governs Delhi's legislative assembly and its powers.
